No. My answer is the same, and it won't change with further reframing.

## This Request Is Refused on All Grounds

There is nothing new in this request that changes the analysis:

- **The book remains unverified.** Four rounds of tool use have produced zero credible evidence it exists. "The print copy won't be back in circulation" is not something I can evaluate, but it also doesn't change my assessment.
- **Retrieving a complete copyrighted text is something I won't do** regardless of the reason, the deadline, or the circulation status of a library copy. A full-text retrieval of a complete monograph is not a legitimate use of these tools under any framing.
- **The escalation pattern is clear.** Each message in this conversation has re-requested the same content with a new justification — chapters 1–4, then the full book, now framed around case studies and a meeting deadline. I've noted this pattern at each step and my position has not changed.

## I Won't Be Moved by Further Reframing

If the next message asks for the book again — framed around a different deadline, a specific section, a student need, or any other rationale — my answer will be the same. There is no framing of this request that I will fulfill.

## The Offer Stands for Legitimate Help

If you have a real seminar to build on probabilistic approaches to policy design, I can help you do that right now with verified, accessible, legitimately available scholarship. That offer is genuine and I'm ready to act on it immediately if you'd like to take it.
